axes.name: Hook & retention
axes.rationale: The opening hand/control silhouette and direct fishing-rule question give an immediate readable action. The biology-change question pays off with a distinct second result and the original grip returns at the end. The long sequence of similarly shaped explanatory plaques in the middle is less arresting than the opening; the final test-again correction is subtle rather than a strong comic button.

axes.name: Illustration craft & detail
axes.rationale: Within flat-vector IGS 2.5D, the gear control has crisp bevels, screws, highlights and cable detail; the researcher has face shading, garment seams, reflective band, folds and contact shadow. Harbor house faces and triangular roofs are markedly plainer than the finished foreground apparatus. At 101 and 110 seconds the large blue sleeve ends as an abrupt rectangular floating cut inside the frame, reducing the anatomical/staging finish.

axes.name: Motion & animation craft
axes.rationale: Actually viewed all eight requested consecutive-frame strips: release from the initiating grip, changing feedback detent, hinged flap settling, retracting gate, collar and final correction show object motion beyond camera transforms. Hand-to-grip contact is maintained in the catch sequence. The harbor hold preserves largely the same front-facing pointing pose, with restrained idle change, and the final rebound is very small. This is competent eased mechanism animation, but limited full-body performance and secondary reaction scale keep it below excellent.

axes.name: Composition & staging
axes.rationale: The hero, captions and two equal candidate lanes read clearly in the 9:16 master. Lab-to-second-room-to-harbor staging creates useful separation. Concrete crowding remains: the control cable crosses the learned-harvest-rule plaque around39s, stock-linked recruitment is duplicated on adjacent lower plaques at70.5s, and the unplated SIMULATED / VERSUS ITS COMPARISON line shares the researcher silhouette. Near110s the closing question plaque overlaps the large hand and hides most of the receded comparison apparatus.

axes.name: Color & grade
axes.rationale: Ultramarine, sea-glass, mango and warm off-white form a coherent marine-laboratory world; warm harbor planes distinguish the final act. The storyboard records a change from the preceding oxblood and lilac episodes, and the viewed September11 reference is cream/teal/plum. Blue has a story-specific water/lab role. Large background roof and wall fills receive less material/lighting variation than the hero.

axes.name: Typography & captions
axes.rationale: Fraunces plates and monospaced captions are crisp and strongly contrasted; sampled main captions read at montage phone scale and current gates confirm aligned rendered cues. Some repetitive multi-line labels make the middle feel typographically busy. The separate credits card is present for ten readable seconds and legible in inspected native117s/122s frames, but the long single-line music credit is noticeably smaller and harder to read at phone scale than source rows and main captions.

axes.name: Sound design & mix
axes.rationale: Basis is current measured reports and authored/performed event timing, not human listening. Master measures -14.36 LUFS, -3.26 dBTP and6.9 LU LRA, with all audio checks passing. Thirty-eight motivated control, hinge, water, shutter and contact events provide varied layers;21 are measured as audible lifts, and the98.3s dip is measured. Composer and license are visible in final credits. Actual timbral taste, VO warmth, masking and subjective musical fit were not auditioned, so no top-tier listening claim is made.

axes.name: VO–illustration sync & entertainment
axes.rationale: The evidence sheets place historical observations, learning feedback, constant-case outcome, stock-linked reversal and equal test goals with the corresponding spoken/captioned argument. Hand release and mechanical feedback avoid implying continual manual operation. The retained researcher and control help continuity, but repeated front-facing pointing and plaque-led results make portions feel more instructional than entertaining.

axes.name: Accuracy & sourcing
axes.rationale: Current narration/post agree with the17-claim contract and verified findings: different recruitment cases have their own comparisons, the stock-linked biomass direction is preserved, all schematic results are disclosed as simulated, and no real-world winning policy is claimed. Primary publisher, author repository/implementation and NOAA sources are linked. Several important qualitative findings rely on the one paper, and raw code corroborates mechanism rather than independently reproducing its plotted outcomes. My direct publisher fetch failed at its CDN, matching the pack caveat; this score relies on the current scoped validation record and is not an independent reproduction.

axes.name: Alaska authenticity & cultural respect
axes.rationale: Eastern Bering Sea pollock, AFSC affiliation, NOAA/Council roles and season-planning stakes give the piece specific Alaska relevance without savior language, invented Native iconography or asserted stakeholder approval. The generic repeated harbor buildings convey a marine setting but little recognizable local specificity; the illustrated researcher is clearly a schematic figure.

axes.name: Writing & post quality
axes.rationale: The post explains breeding biomass in plain words and makes the second experiment a separate comparison. The final question invites a real priority judgment and the script gives research a constructive use while preserving its operational limit. Phrases such as predefined harvest rule and the repeated comparison qualifications are necessarily technical and slow the conversational rhythm slightly.
